holidays.name: Lima Bean Respect Day
holidays.description: Today the humble lima bean gets the admiration it has long been denied. Cook up some succotash, toss butter beans into a stew, or just stop making a face at them. This is the day to give the most-maligned bean on the dinner plate a second chance.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It seems to have started as a lighthearted push to improve the lima bean's reputation.
holidays.funFact: Lima beans are named after Lima, Peru, and have been cultivated in the Americas for thousands of years. In the American South they are often called butter beans.

holidays.name: National Look Alike Day
holidays.description: Dress up, strike a pose, and find your twin, whether that's a celebrity, a cartoon character, or your own best friend. It's a day for celebrity doppelgängers and for pairs who just happen to look alike. Matching outfits are encouraged, and so are double takes.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a popular fixture on April calendars and is a fun excuse for costumes and selfies.
holidays.funFact: Researchers have studied look-alikes, who are unrelated people with strikingly similar faces. Some of these pairs even turn out to share genetic similarities.

holidays.name: National Cheddar Fries Day
holidays.description: French fries get smothered in melty, gooey cheddar cheese today. Load them up with bacon, scallions, or chili, or keep them simple with a cheese sauce drizzle. It's a salty, cheesy tribute to one of the great snack pairings.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It's part of the long list of days that celebrate fast-food favorites.
holidays.funFact: Cheese fries are a cousin of Canada's poutine, which also pairs fries with cheese, though poutine adds gravy and uses cheese curds.
